modelName: CT unwrapped-diagram and SSPz geometry reference
purpose: Visualize acquired-row geometry separately from an ideal axial response using Taguchi and Aradate (1998) Eq. (6) rectangular filter interpolation. The response fixes a thin object and moves the reconstruction plane; 360 curves change the object position within one helical table feed. This is not complete image reconstruction or scanner-specific nominal-thickness prediction.

referenceImplementation.note: Historical baseline only: the named Python reference and full-scan fixture use the former fixed-plane candidate-kernel model. They do not validate the current thick-slice response. Current longitudinal filtering follows Taguchi Eq. (6): reselect adjacent acquired candidates at every resampling z position, linearly interpolate, then apply the normalized finite rectangular-weight sum. Geometry and row apertures remain idealized; complete FBP, scanner-specific weights, and finite bead diameter are excluded.

literatureBackground.role: Conceptual basis for transverse-position-dependent SSP variation in spiral CT.
literatureBackground.implementationBoundary: The original 180-degree half-scan formulation is not directly implemented.

literatureBackground.role: Conceptual basis for angular-longitudinal SSP analysis in multi-row-detector spiral CT.
literatureBackground.implementationBoundary: The declared acquisition-geometry model applies the fan-beam complementary angle, its two acquired angular neighbors, generalized two-point longitudinal interpolation, and their linear angular combination. Scanner-specific opposing-ray synthesis, redundancy weighting, z filtering, and backprojection are not implemented.

literatureBackground.role: Theoretical background for longitudinal interpolation and normalized weighting in multislice spiral CT.
literatureBackground.implementationBoundary: The adaptive axial interpolator is not implemented.

literatureBackground.role: Theoretical background for helical cone-beam reconstruction and data-use considerations.
literatureBackground.implementationBoundary: The exact and approximate reconstruction algorithms are not implemented; the web distance scaling is an idealized geometry display.

literatureBackground.role: Primary longitudinal filtering source: Eq. (6), Figs. 5/6, local resampling with adjacent linear interpolation and a normalized rectangular filter.
literatureBackground.implementationBoundary: Only the longitudinal filter-interpolation construction is implemented on the declared idealized acquisition geometry and row-aperture samples. Optimized-pitch selection, complete original FBP, scanner-specific weights, and nominal-thickness calibration are not reproduced.

literatureBackground.role: Basis for interlaced direct/complementary helical samples and generalized two-point linear interpolation using the measurements nearest the target plane across detector rows.
literatureBackground.implementationBoundary: The all-row direct/complementary candidate union is used in the primary explanatory SSPz; scanner-specific redundancy handling, z-filter design, and backprojection are not.

literatureBackground.role: Basis for complementary-ray fan-beam geometry and for recognizing the limitation of exact complementary rays in three-dimensional cone-beam geometry.
literatureBackground.implementationBoundary: The model remains an idealized acquisition-geometry reference and does not implement missing-data restoration.

scanCalculationConvention: Direct views cover 0 <= beta < 360 degrees. Fan-beam complementary angles use beta+180 degrees+2gamma and their two acquired angular neighbors. Each local resampling coordinate z_f has its own direct/complementary adjacent-candidate selection and normalized linear weights. Angular branches are convexly combined and K resampling values equally averaged. The thin object and its acquired row-aperture samples remain fixed while the reconstruction plane z_r moves. Linear aggregation of the rebracketed piecewise-linear response is used before the finite shifted sum; this is not postconvolution of the former fixed-plane candidate kernel. T is used only as a reference thickness for reported ratios. The direct-only comparator omits complementary samples but uses the same moving-plane/filter response definition.
angleConvention: The diagram uses a model-relative tube angle beta with 0 degrees at the top and 360 degrees at the bottom. It is not a measured absolute tube angle. The drawn endpoint at 360 degrees closes the displayed helix period but is not double-counted in SSPz integration.
overlayConvention: The overlay samples 360 fixed-object positions within one table feed. Each curve fixes that object and moves the reconstruction plane, is individually peak-normalized, and uses z_reconstruction-z_object without peak or centroid alignment. All states and all calculated z samples are rendered. Center panels share a >=10% derived horizontal domain; the cone-on log-tail panel uses values >=0.1%. Display thresholds do not truncate the calculated or exported response.
candidateDisplayConvention: The all-N-row direct and complementary acquired-view trajectories and geometric coordinates are unchanged. Cone-off uses q=1 and a 180-degree complementary angle; cone-on uses fan-angle correspondence and each acquired family's own distance scaling. T and FW do not remove the displayed row population. Section 2B markers/weights and Section 2C gaps refer to local FW=0 interpolation at the selected central position, not all acquired samples contributing across a thick-slice filter. The geometry reference plane passes through the object position selected for SSPz. Same acquired samples may reappear in different angular correspondences; displayed counts are not independent data counts.
acquisitionGeometryFigureConvention: The Section 3C introductory figure is a pre-weight acquisition-geometry display for the currently inspected state. It shows a not-to-scale orthographic focal-spot helix, target plane, one direct acquired view, the two acquired complementary views bracketing the ideal beta plus 180 degrees plus 2 gamma angle, and every detector-row center mapped to the longitudinal line through the evaluation point. Nine representative row rays are drawn in the 3-D panel only for legibility; the adjacent longitudinal panel and numerical calculation retain all rows. A physical detector plane is not inferred because detector-to-isocenter distance is not an input. Color, opacity, and line width encode geometric role only. Circle and triangle markers identify candidates nearest the target plane for explanation; they do not assert use or weight. Schaller AAI h(z), weight normalization, filtering, and backprojection are not applied in this figure.
weightDisplayConvention: Section 2B fixed-size circle/triangle markers and saturation encode normalized local FW=0 endpoint weights at the selected central plane, including angular branch weights. They are not the aggregated thick-slice filter weights. Equal-z ties share endpoint weight as an explicit idealized convention.
allCandidateAxialSpreadConvention: For every direct acquired view beta, the candidate set contains all N detector-row centres in that direct view and all N row centres in each distinct acquired view immediately below and above the ideal complementary angle. A repeated lower-and-upper physical view is included only once, yielding 2N points for an exactly acquired complementary angle and 3N points otherwise. If z-k are the candidate positions, z-bar is their arithmetic mean, and M is their count, the displayed value is sqrt(sum((z-k minus z-bar) squared)/M) in millimetres. It uses no interpolation weight, nearest-candidate selection, support threshold, detector-row aperture variance, or configured slice thickness T. The value is invariant under a common longitudinal translation, so reconstruction-plane position s is not repeated as a second axis. The off/on curves use the same beta and millimetre axes.
internalCandidateAuditConvention: The former computeSsp fixed-plane kernel remains a local-FW0 geometry/legacy numerical diagnostic. Its moments and selected-candidate counts are not interpreted as all thick-slice contributors and are not exported as filtered-response variances.
momentConvention: The former mean(M2)+T^2/12 identity belongs only to the historical fixed-plane-kernel plus continuous width-T rectangle model. It is not an acceptance identity for the fixed-object moving-plane response or the finite-K Taguchi filter. Current filtered width and standard-deviation outputs are computed from the new response.
numericalRasterizationConvention: The current fixed-object response evaluates acquired ideal row apertures and adjacent interpolation as a piecewise-linear function of reconstruction-plane z, combines angular views by linearity, and evaluates the finite K shifted resampling sum. The output grid is shared across states and cone conditions; the requested count is a minimum. No T-wide post-average or old fixed-plane profile rasterization is used to form the new default output. Numerical acceptance requires comparison to direct per-view, per-z, per-filter-position evaluation and K/grid convergence.
complementaryPairConvention: The primary 180LI SSPz path is exact only within the declared idealized acquisition model. Its continuous complementary angle uses the second intersection of the source-to-evaluation-point line with the source orbit. For each acquired angular neighbor, all direct-side and complementary-side detector-row samples are merged and the adjacent candidates around each local z_f are used, allowing DD, DC, CD, or CC types while retaining equal-distance ties and exact matches. The two branch kernels are combined by the ideal angle's linear fraction between the acquired neighbors. The absolute-order D-n-to-C-n and C-n-to-D-n-plus-one spans remain separate diagnostics and are not averaged as an unvalidated redundancy rule. Scanner-specific detector-channel interpolation, redundancy weights, cone-beam weights, z-filter calibration, and backprojection remain outside scope.

filterInterpolation.filterSamplesMeaning: requested minimum odd count; actual K may increase and is recorded separately
filterInterpolation.filterSamplesAccuracyGuard: FW/K <= rowWidth*(1-radius/sourceRadius)/8; required odd K > 2049 causes a precision-limit error with no result
filterInterpolation.operation: At each z_f, reselect adjacent acquired direct/complementary row samples in each angular branch, linearly interpolate, combine angular branches, and average K values equally. Acquired candidates outside FW can be used to bracket positions inside FW.
filterInterpolation.thicknessMapping: FW and T are independent; no FWHM fit or scanner calibration
filterInterpolation.legacyInitialization: Missing FW takes the initial numerical value T; this is explicitly uncalibrated, not a FW=T identity.
